Keysight Technologies Inc operates within the Technology sector with a forward price to earnings of 20.6612 and a trailing price to earnings of 45.8862 [N]. The company reported revenue of $1.85 billion for the third quarter ended July 31, 2026, which represents a growth on a year earlier of 0.365385 according to the filing [D1]. GAAP net income was $397 million or $2.30 per share compared with $191 million or $1.10 per share in the third quarter of 2025 as stated in the results release [D1]. Non-GAAP net income was $531 million or $3.07 per share compared with $297 million or $1.72 per share in the third quarter of 2025 according to the filing [D1]. Cash flow from operations was $437 million compared to $322 million last year as reported in the document [D1]. Free cash flow was $403 million compared to $291 million in the third quarter of 2025 per the company filing [D1]. As of July 31, 2026, cash, cash equivalents, and restricted cash totaled $2.62 billion according to the results release [D1].

Orders were $2.091 billion which is up 56% on a reported basis as stated by Executive VP & CFO Neil Dougherty in the earnings call summary [D3]. Revenue of $1.846 billion was up 36% on a reported basis per the executive vice president and chief financial officer [D3]. The company delivered net income of $531 million and earnings per share of $3.07 as confirmed by the executive vice president and chief financial officer [D3]. Gross margin was 69% and operating expenses were $661 million according to the executive vice president and chief financial officer [D3]. Within the Communications Solutions Group, the Commercial Communications business generated its first $1 billion quarter with revenue of $1.006 billion up 56% led by outstanding growth in wireline and supported by strong growth in wireless per the executive vice president and chief financial officer [D3]. Wireline revenue exceeded wireless revenue for the first time this quarter as noted by the executive vice president and chief financial officer [D3].

The earnings reaction to the latest report date of 2026-08-19 showed a move per cent of -6.319648 with an actual earnings reaction of 2.82 against an estimate of 2.16 [N]. The latest quarter earnings per share growth on a year earlier was 0.639535 and the latest quarter revenue growth on a year earlier was 0.365385 [N]. Management raised their outlook for Q4 and for the full fiscal year as stated by President, CEO & Director Satish Dhanasekaran in the earnings call insights [D3]. For the fourth quarter of 2026, the company expects revenue in the range of $1.930 billion to $1.950 billion per the executive vice president and chief financial officer [D3]. We expect Q4 earnings per share to be in the range of $3.34 to $3.40 according to the executive vice president and chief financial officer [D3]. This will result in fiscal year 2026 revenue growth of 32% and EPS growth of approximately 60% at the midpoint as stated by the executive vice president and chief financial officer [D3].

Analysts' tone was slightly negative to pressing on sustainability and constraints with repeated probing on demand durability and fulfillment including questions on whether demand is sustainable per Mark Delaney of Goldman Sachs in the earnings call summary [D3]. Management's tone was positive in prepared remarks and more guarded in Q&A around constraints repeatedly returning to supply as a limiter including far exceeding our ability to supply per President, CEO & Director Satish Dhanasekaran [D3]. The supply environment is less flexible today than let's say a year ago according to President, CEO & Director Satish Dhanasekaran [D3]. Supply chain will remain the governor of near-term revenue as stated by President, CEO & Director Satish Dhanasekaran [D3]. The only thing I would just caution people to pay attention to is we did have the onetime tariff impacts this year that won't repeat per Executive VP & CFO Neil Dougherty [D3].
